target_customer: Engineering and operations teams at companies that want internal AI agents and workflows built by coding agents
problem: Visual workflow tools get hard to maintain at scale and code-first frameworks leave teams to build hosting, chat UI and permissions themselves.
business_model: Usage-based platform with free starter credits (open alpha, open source core)
product_category: Developer tools, internal agent and workflow platform

founders.name: Blake Rouse
prior_employers: DataSpark (bootstrapped analytics startup, later acquired by Threecolts)
education: BYU, product management and computer science, dropped out after three years
founders.background_notes: Led product development at DataSpark per YC profile

founders.name: Dallin Bentley
founders.background_notes: YC profile lists only an AI focus

technical_complexity.rationale: Text-to-SQL analyst agents on dbt projects were standard LLM engineering with hard parts around accuracy and warehouse integration. The later Keystroke platform adds hosting, permissions and chat UI, which is typical product engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Open source core and a founder statement that Cursor rebuilt the Buster agent in about five minutes show how copyable agent code is. No data or network moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Warehouse vendors shipped native AI analyst features (Snowflake Cortex Analyst appears in 2025 roundups). Nothing sourced on actions against Keystroke itself.

market_need_then: Business users wanted plain English data questions answered without analysts; the founders then found internal agent tooling painful while building their own, per the Launch YC post. No spend figures found.

branding.domain_note: Uses keystroke.ai; the original Buster product used buster.so. The keystroke.ai root returned 404 when fetched.

identity.mascot_or_character: Internal agent named Delbert (the Buster-era agent)

rebrands.why: Pivot from AI data analyst to internal agents platform; date approximate from the Launch YC page, which shows relative time only

branding.community_and_virality: Open source on GitHub and a Launch YC post; no merch or fan activity found.

brand_strength.rationale: Two names in two years, generic term, little press about the brand itself.

pivots.from: Buster, an AI data analyst for dbt projects
pivots.to: Keystroke, open source platform for internal agents and workflows
pivots.why: Founders found visual tools hard to maintain and code-first tools missing hosting and UI while building agents for Buster; exact date not sourced

outcome_analysis: Keystroke is active and early. The company went through YC W24 as Buster, an AI data analyst, raised a reported 2.4 million dollar seed in April 2025 from YC and General Catalyst, then pivoted to an open source internal agents platform that is in open alpha. It is too early to call an outcome, and the pivot suggests the first idea did not produce a clear market position.
notes: The $2.4M seed was raised under the Buster brand (company blog dated 2025-04-21, cross-checked by startups.gallery and Caplight, both aggregators). Aggregators also list about $500K pre-seed in 2024, unverified so not recorded as a round. No competitor source dated near January 2024 was found, so the list is empty. Pivot date and Launch YC date are approximate.
